courses.name: Data Structures & Algorithms
courses.curriculum_text: Arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, and graphs; asymptotic (Big-O) analysis; recursion and divide-and-conquer; sorting algorithms (quicksort, mergesort, heapsort) and their tradeoffs; hash tables and collision handling; binary search trees and balanced trees (AVL/red-black); graph traversal (BFS/DFS), shortest paths (Dijkstra), and minimum spanning trees; dynamic programming; amortized analysis. Weekly problem sets implemented in a systems language.

courses.name: Object-Oriented Programming
courses.curriculum_text: Classes, objects, encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism; interfaces and abstract classes; design patterns (factory, observer, strategy, singleton); UML class and sequence diagrams; SOLID principles; unit testing and test-driven development; exception handling; basic memory management and object lifecycle. Team project building a mid-sized application with version control.

courses.name: Database Management Systems
courses.curriculum_text: Relational model and relational algebra; ER modeling and schema design; SQL (joins, subqueries, aggregation, window functions); normalization (1NF–BCNF) and denormalization tradeoffs; indexing and query execution plans; transactions, ACID properties, and isolation levels; concurrency control and locking; basics of query optimization; introduction to NoSQL and when to reach for it. Semester project designing and querying a multi-table schema.

courses.name: Operating Systems
courses.curriculum_text: Process and thread management; CPU scheduling algorithms; synchronization primitives (mutexes, semaphores, condition variables) and classic concurrency problems; deadlock detection and prevention; virtual memory and paging; file systems and I/O; inter-process communication; an introduction to system calls. Labs implemented in C against a Unix-like kernel.

courses.name: Computer Networks
courses.curriculum_text: The OSI and TCP/IP models; addressing and routing; the transport layer (TCP vs UDP, congestion control); the application layer (HTTP, DNS, email protocols); socket programming; network security fundamentals (TLS, firewalls); an introduction to distributed systems concepts (latency, partition tolerance). Labs build a simple client-server application over sockets.

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.curriculum_text: Supervised learning: linear and logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, support vector machines; unsupervised learning: k-means clustering, PCA; model evaluation (train/test split, cross-validation, precision/recall/F1, ROC curves); feature engineering and feature selection; regularization and the bias-variance tradeoff; an introduction to neural networks and gradient descent; the linear algebra and probability underpinning the above. Coursework in Python using standard ML libraries; final project trains and evaluates a model on a real dataset.

courses.name: Web Development
courses.curriculum_text: HTTP fundamentals and the request/response cycle; client-server architecture; building REST APIs (routing, request validation, status codes, authentication basics); frontend UI implementation with a component-based framework; state management on the client; responsive layout with CSS; connecting a frontend to a backend and a database; an introduction to deployment. Semester project ships a full-stack CRUD application.

courses.name: Software Engineering
courses.curriculum_text: The software development lifecycle; requirements gathering and specification; software architecture and design patterns; version control workflows (branching, code review); unit, integration, and system testing; CI/CD pipelines; agile methodology (sprints, standups, retrospectives); technical debt and refactoring; basics of software project estimation. Team project run as a semester-long sprint cycle with a real stakeholder.

courses.name: Probability & Statistics
courses.curriculum_text: Probability axioms, conditional probability, and Bayes' theorem; discrete and continuous random variables and common distributions; expectation and variance; the central limit theorem; point estimation and confidence intervals; hypothesis testing and p-values; correlation and simple linear regression; an introduction to A/B testing and experimental design. Problem sets combine hand calculation with statistical software.

courses.name: Computer Vision
courses.curriculum_text: Image formation and digital image representation; filtering and convolution; edge and feature detection; image segmentation; classical object detection and recognition techniques; an introduction to convolutional neural networks for vision tasks; camera calibration and basic geometric vision; dataset labeling and augmentation. Final project trains a vision model on a labeled image dataset.
